the adipose tissue secretome plays a major role in breast cancer aggressiveness, especially in terms of resistance to endocrine treatment.

the secretome adipocyte could be implicated in the increased mortality observed in obese patients with breast cancer by reducing the efficacy of anti-cancer treatments such as Tamoxifen and could also play a role in the behavior of breast cancer stem cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity is a risk factor for breast cancer and that the secretome adipocytaire plays a role in the progression of breast cancer and in the response to hormonal treatments.

the adipocyte secretome may be involved in the increased mortality rate observed in obese patients with breast cancer by decreasing the efficacy of anti-cancer treatments such as tamoxifen and by promoting the proliferation of breast cancer stem cells.

adipose tissue is not only a reservoir of energy but it is also a source of paracrine factors that can influence the behavior of cancer cells and that may be involved in the development of resistance to anti cancer treatments.
